title: SAT Words in Context: Answer Without Knowing the Word
description:
SAT Words in Context questions give you a short passage with a blank (or a word in the passage) and four choices, and some of those words you might not know. You can still get them right. This video shows how to predict your own word from the clue before you look, eliminate by charge, and choose the most precise fit.

You'll learn:
• How to find the clue: restatement, contrast, cause and effect
• Negation traps like "far from"
• Predicting your own word before looking at the choices
• Eliminating by charge (positive, negative, neutral)
• Precision and tone: near-synonyms that are too strong or too weak
• Secondary meanings of common words (qualified, check, novel, sanction)
• What to do when the right answer is a word you don't know

All practice questions in this video are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (filter: Craft and Structure, Words in Context).
